items.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: That was a thing that Charlie Mingus put out on Debut Records... I had Louie Bellson on drums, Percy Heath and who else, Urbie Green and Bob Dorough... So anyhow, so my friend brought it to Charlie Mingus, he liked it and he put it out.

ctx.x: I was playing flute. Yeah, I think maybe the whole record was a flute thing. And then shortly after that, well I think it was in 1954, I’m talking about this guy that was kind of pushing my career, we got into the studio and I don’t know exactly how it is, maybe he put up the money or I put up the money, we got a thing called “Sam Most Plus Two.” I don’t know if you’re familiar with that. That was a thing that Charlie Mingus put out on Debut Records. Now what happened was I had Louie Bellson on drums, Percy Heath…

items.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Charles Mingus called you the world’s greatest jazz flute player. ... he put out that album

ctx.x: I listen to a lot of the people like Hubert Laws and Joe Farrell. In fact most of my influence has been more like saxophone players you see. So that’s why I associate the bebop thing and the style plus my own whatever I do with those influences. So it seems like I listen to more saxophone players than flutists. I like a lot of these people. I was just more influenced by Charlie Parker and Stan Getz and Lee Konitz, that type of thing.
You had some pretty nice compliments from — Charles Mingus called you the world’s greatest jazz flute player.
Yeah, well don’t forget he put out that album—
